relation_rules.reason: Session persistence owner may append turn truth under the persisted session.
Session persistence owner may project persisted session index and metadata to UI-safe list/search DTOs while UI remains read-only.
Turn execution may enter the context planner to derive provider-neutral request context.
The live bridge may build provider request truth from typed request context.
Provider semantic may carry hosted search as provider-neutral request metadata without making it a Freehand function tool.
The live bridge and provider adapters may select and render hosted search only through provider request truth and declared provider capabilities.
Reason turn owner may apply normalized provider semantic output into turn truth.
Provider adapters may map hosted search response items into provider-neutral observations without routing through local tool execution.
UI protocol owns the input attachment DTO contract and may reject unsupported or incomplete attachment metadata before runtime dispatch.
Runtime command dispatch may carry current-submit image payloads into provider-neutral request metadata exactly once while keeping raw bytes out of persisted session history.
Runtime may project metadata-only attachment rows into UI protocol so uploaded images remain observable after refresh without rehydrating raw payloads.
Provider adapters may render current-submit provider-neutral image attachments into their private wire DTOs; runtime must not hardcode the wire shape.
Tool registry owner may execute governed workspace path operations for a tool call.
Tool registry owner may execute a bounded HTTP/HTTPS fetch for a concrete URL and return only tool-result text/error truth.
Tool registry owner may expose UI-safe built-in schema, examples, guidance, scope, and exposure metadata without executing tools or leaking provider-hosted search as a local function tool.
Runtime UI command dispatch may project UI-safe diagnostics metadata and redacted log tails from debug trace truth without exposing raw provider payloads, secrets, or absolute user paths.
Provider-hosted search is declared and observed through provider request/response truth; it must not be implemented as a local Freehand function-tool execution.
Task owner truth may be projected into UI protocol without UI owning task state.
A task may persist one immutable creation parent plus explicit observing-session attachments so current-session progress is visible without assigning the agent to the session.
Task orchestration may create or replace a temporary assignment to an available agent while the agent remains a reusable pool resource.
Task orchestration owns task lifecycle mutation and may cancel a non-terminal task without routing through another resource.
Session-to-agent attachment is a derived current-progress projection through task parent and assignment truth; sessions never own agents directly.
Agent lifecycle owner may update one agent's typed process identity and heartbeat projection without a second health resource.
The Worker runner may read AgentLifecycle truth and derive one ephemeral typed control activity projection; it may not write UI or ADP payloads.
Runtime may derive direct-session activity from active-turn truth into the same typed control projection without mutating turn or UI truth.
The daemon host may map the typed runtime activity projection into Relay control heartbeat status/count only; business payload copying is forbidden.
Due timers inject a persisted wakeup prompt as a new source-session turn when source truth exists, or use an internal wakeup turn when source-less.
The timer owner may schedule and cancel independent timer truth inside the timer schedule store and ledger without Task Center state.
The timer owner may expose UI-safe schedule and ledger projections through protocol DTOs without making WebUI or Task Center the timer truth owner.
The Master lifecycle owner may persist only typed changed-task identity and decision kind from an isolated Task Center attention outcome into the active-work return contract.

The runtime Master lifecycle owner may convert one validated typed attention resolution into a volatile no-cache context segment; final ordering and provider request construction still pass through the request-context planner.
Error center may record classified error truth through metadata owner constraints.
Writable workspace path effects must create checkpoint truth before mutation.
Runtime rewind commands route to checkpoint owner instead of mutating workspace paths directly.
Config owner may validate and atomically replace its own provider registry, model group registry, and agent selection truth without routing through another resource.
Config owner compiles account-scoped remote daemon, endpoint candidate, route selection, and bootstrap truth before node or client surfaces consume it.
Config truth compiles the reciprocal Master/Worker peer topology; node pairing may materialize only relations present in that compiled topology.
Node owner may consume config-compiled account and endpoint truth to publish one account-scoped multi-daemon directory and route resolution without owning configuration or credential truth.
Relay account owner may register credentials and authenticate opaque token hashes without exposing raw secrets to config, daemon, WebUI, or Android owners.
Relay presence owner may persist authenticated heartbeats and derive account-scoped online/offline directory projections from lease freshness.
An authenticated Agent identity must enter transport through the control tunnel that owns its presence lifecycle.
A data tunnel may be admitted only after the same account and Agent identity has an active control tunnel.
An error tunnel may be admitted only by the same registry mutation that observes the account and Agent identity's active control tunnel.
The Relay Agent client may enter the outbound lifecycle only by establishing its authenticated control identity before dependent channel admission.
The independent Relay data tunnel owns opaque HTTP and ADP exchange IO only and cannot become config, node, session, task, provider, or Android truth.
The typed Relay error owner may close exactly one authenticated pending data exchange and deliver its explicit failure without entering business payload bytes.
Android owns only package update checking, APK cache download, and system-installer handoff for its installed package; daemon release distribution remains served by the selected endpoint.
Android owns only its package runtime permission request, all-files settings handoff, and startup permission status logging; file operation semantics remain with their existing owners.
Android owns only notification permission, turn-finished notification posting, duplicate suppression, tap return intent, and status logging for its package.
The WebUI app boundary may render protocol-owned projections into ephemeral shell and surface DOM without becoming session, task, lifecycle, or config truth.
UI protocol may bind generated ADP frame constructors to request-id-correlated response/failure projection without creating a second truth owner.
The daemon-hosted WebUI may call the Android notification bridge only from protocol turn projection truth after observing a live same-turn terminal transition.
Node pairing owner may publish status/progress/slave-turn projections through UI protocol.
Config-owned instruction sources may compile into deterministic instruction capability manifests.
UI may dispatch commands and read projections, but must not mutate or parse task truth directly.
Global session lists must show persisted session metadata, not temporary turn-only worker sessions.
Waiting and wakeup are independent timer resources; task lifecycle state must not encode timer schedules.
Turns must build provider requests through typed context planning, not by ad hoc prompt/provider payload rewrites.
Workspace restore commands must pass through checkpoint truth before mutating workspace paths.
Metadata may observe provenance and control watermarks, but must not recover or mutate request-context payload truth directly.
Instruction capabilities may become model-visible only through typed context-planner admission, not provider payload patching.
Instruction capability owner output may enter provider-visible context only by constructing a typed InstructionCapability context segment for the context planner.
UI may render node pairing projections and dispatch commands, but must not own or mutate node pairing transport truth directly.
ACP session/prompt drives one live-reason turn through the runtime master-work mainline; ACP owns the transport, not the turn truth.
Runtime master-work broadcast events are projected into ACP session/update notifications by the app.acp-server adapter; acp_transport owns the wire, not the runtime truth.
relay.transport is the single HTTP projection owner for deployment-staged update bytes; it does not build or mutate the release artifact

config.account-config-sync owns schema validation, revision/etag lifecycle, atomic persistence, and safe projection of the account-scoped versioned document; relay.transport provides only the authenticated account boundary
config.core owns the local-to-shared projection boundary and may call the account-config schema validator/export surface without moving credentials or whole config truth
